jobs.title: General Opening
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Not found a job opening that suits right now? We would still like to hear from you.

Our General Opening is an opportunity for experienced academics, technologists, and product professionals to speculatively apply to us during their job search.

We are interested in hearing from you if your profile aligns with one of the following areas:

  • Experienced technologists & researchers: You have deep expertise in our relevant fields, and are driven to build complex systems from first principles.

  • Product professionals: You have experience launching or scaling products in a deep-tech "lab to customer" environment. You excel at identifying high-value use cases (particularly within the financial, investment, or physics sectors) and defining the commercial path for complex technologies.

Within your application please tell us about your experiences within our relevant areas of work. The more information we receive the better assessment we can make on your profile to hopefully move forward to the interviewing process. On receiving your application we will review and assess whether there is an opportunity for us to work together. If it does not work out this time, we will gladly reach back out to you when job openings become available that suit your skill set.

  • Check out a list of skill sets we constantly look for on our Join Us page.

  • Prior to applying, why not learn more about our Goal, Technology and Ways of Work by looking through our website and YouTube channel. You can also find some typical tasks that we have across different areas and technologies on our Example Tasks page.

    • What we do: https://planting.space/

    • Ways of work: https://planting.space/org/

jobs.title: Technical Project Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We're building a system that represents domain knowledge as modular probabilistic models — making analysis rigorous and transparent. Users can connect these models flexibly into larger structures. The system enforces consistency across them, and propagates uncertainty through each step. Our first applications are in finance and scientific research, with use cases ranging from equity valuation and distress monitoring, to particle physics.

We are looking for a Technical Project Manager to bridge the gap between strategic planning and hands-on development. You will help to manage our roadmap and refine our engineering processes. This is a role for someone with software engineering experience combined with organisational instinct, who thrives in a fast-paced environment; you will work alongside a highly collaborative engineering and product team, balancing strategic priorities and complex challenges, with rapid high-quality execution.

 

Useful experience

  • Software engineering in a collaborative, commercial environment, working on large codebases and using practices like CI/CD, testing, and code reviews.

  • Functional/typed languages, e.g. Rust, OCaml, Clojure, C++, or Haskell, and a willingness to learn and work with Julia.

  • Implementation of pragmatic organisational processes.

  • Background in Technical Product Management, working with complex technical systems.

  • Coordination of workflows across multiple contributors and topics

Responsibilities

  • Manage the development roadmap: Work with leadership as well as individual contributors, to identify interdependencies, and adapt to shifts in priorities and timelines as goals are achieved. Day to day, this includes writing, consolidating, and triaging tasks that come out of discussions and planning.

  • Drive quarterly planning: Initiate and prepare reviews; identify potential goal owners early and flag planning risks and dependencies before they become blockers.

  • Steer features from idea to implementation: Coordinate work from idea to implementation; track work across multiple topics, when a new feature idea comes up, ensure it progresses from product specification, design, and prioritisation, through to implementation, bridging gaps between different technical and product areas.

  • Maintain technical documentation and tooling: Reviewing frequently and coordinating updates, and improve our internal technical processes.

  • Facilitate communication: Be a responsive point of contact across our channels, connecting team members with the right information and resources.

  • Develop hands-on: Build tools and automations that support the team's workflow.

Questions candidates typically ask

  • What does progression look like? You start by working closely with our technical co-founder on the concrete work of planning and coordination, and grow from there. There is no fixed ladder; as you show what you can carry, you take on more, and we actively help you get there. The responsibilities above are the direction.

  • What does success look like? You will thrive here if you find satisfaction in the careful, behind-the-scenes work that keeps a team moving. You can assess your own abilities well, and want to earn scope rather than be granted it. You will struggle if you need a defined territory and formal authority to be able to operate.

  • What does failure look like? The pattern that has led to failure in the past is: many threads opened and few brought to completion, tasks talked bigger instead of broken down smaller, process ideas raised without a demonstrated pain point, claims defended instead of explored, and blockers left uncommunicated until someone else has to step in.

How we work

  • Hierarchical goals, not personal hierarchies: We organise around a transparent tree of goals and tasks. Every quarter we plan milestone goals, which branch down into smaller and smaller tasks. This tree is the foundation of how we organise, not a side tool.

  • Transparency: Everyone should have access to every opportunity in the team that they can realistically handle. All goals, tasks, and the reasoning behind them are visible to everyone.

  • Decisions become tasks: When something is discussed and decided, it gets captured as a task in the right place in the tree, so that nothing dissipates as hot air. In this role, that instinct is your daily bread.

  • Written and asynchronous by default: We are fully remote and document naturally. If you learned something, you write it down for the next person. Communication happens transparently in shared channels, not in private threads and one-on-ones.

  • Growing from leaf to tree: New joiners start from smaller leaves of the tree and work themselves up to ownership of larger branches as trust and understanding build. Teams form around topics and dissolve when the work is done; people move to where they are most useful.

Want to know more?

On our website you can find more about our team and work culture, as well as example tasks that share some insight into the type of things team members are working on.

  • What we do: https://planting.space/

  • Ways of work: https://planting.space/org/

  • Team culture and example tasks: https://planting.space/joinus/

Our team works fully remotely, and mostly within the CET timezone.

jobs.title: Quantitative Modelling Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We are building a system that represents domain knowledge as modular probabilistic models. Users compose them into larger structures, the system enforces consistency across them, and uncertainty is propagated across model boundaries autonomously by the composition itself.

You will implement models that our users need, inside of our framework. Our current applications range from equity valuation and financial distress monitoring to particle physics.

The interesting part is not any single model. It is that the same compositional machinery has to carry models from very different domains (finance, physics, others) without special-casing any of them. That generality is the hard part of the design, and it is what we are building toward.

What you will do

  • Work with the product team to define what a model needs to do, then own it through to something a user can run

  • Define and document the implementation approach for harder modelling problems

  • Write code that is clean enough to be maintained by others and fast enough to run at the scale users need

  • Establish that a model is correct, not just that it executes

  • Find where the framework constrains the model you are trying to build, and feed that back concretely enough to act on

  • Contribute to the surrounding production system

Useful experience

  • Taking models into production for external users and remaining accountable for their correctness in use

  • Applied mathematical modelling in finance and/or scientific applications

  • Strong foundation in computer science algorithms and data structures

  • Experience in a collaborative, commercial software engineering environment, working on large codebases and using practices like CI/CD, testing, and code reviews

  • Julia, or usage of some more functional or typed languages, e.g. Rust, OCaml, Clojure, C++, or Haskell

  • Profiling and performance optimisation

  • Advanced degree in Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, or Statistics

Where you might be coming from

  • Scientific or engineering software, where you implemented solvers or physical models into a product with external users

  • A risk or analytics vendor, where you built the model library itself rather than configuring it for clients

  • A research background in a computational field, followed by several years shipping in a commercial product team

How we work

  • Hierarchical goals, not personal hierarchies: We organise around a transparent tree of goals and tasks. Every quarter we plan milestone goals, which branch down into smaller and smaller tasks. This tree is the foundation of how we organise, not a side tool.

  • Transparency: Everyone should have access to every opportunity in the team that they can realistically handle. All goals, tasks, and the reasoning behind them are visible to everyone.

  • Decisions become tasks: When something is discussed and decided, it gets captured as a task in the right place in the tree, so that nothing dissipates as hot air.

  • Written and asynchronous by default: We are fully remote and document our learnings in writing. Communication happens transparently in shared channels, not in private threads and one-on-ones.

  • Growing from leaf to tree: New joiners start from smaller leaves of the tree and work themselves up to ownership of larger branches as trust and understanding build. Teams form around topics and dissolve when the work is done; people move to where they are most useful.

On our website you can find more about our team and work culture, as well as example tasks that share some insight into the type of things team members are working on.

jobs.title: Domain Expert Partnerships
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We're building a system that represents domain knowledge as modular probabilistic models — making analysis rigorous and transparent by design. Users can connect these models flexibly into larger structures. The system enforces consistency across them, and propagates uncertainty through every step. Our first applications are in finance and scientific research, with use cases ranging from equity valuation and distress monitoring, to particle physics.

We are seeking domain experts to collaborate with us on developing high-value use cases that leverage our system’s unique capabilities. Rather than acting as traditional consultants; we need builders and practitioners who are ready to integrate these solutions directly into pilot users’ workflows, drawing on their established industry networks to drive real-world adoption.

Your profile

  • Deep domain expertise — You are a current or former practitioner with hands-on experience solving complex problems in your field

  • Technical understanding — You possess a strong grasp of statistical modeling, enabling close collaboration with our engineers on developing solutions

  • Industry connections — You bring a network of relevant contacts, to identify and engage as pilot users

Your field of expertise

We are actively seeking to develop:

  • Valuation Modes

  • Quantitative Default-Probability Models

  • Interest Rate Prediction Models

  • …and more within the Financial Analysis space

What Makes a Viable Use Case

Problem Characteristics:

  • No existing AI solution — Problems currently handled mostly manually or through custom programming by engineering teams

  • Clear pain points in current solutions — E.g., existing approaches (Excel models, custom programs) are brittle, hard to validate, don't integrate varied data sources easily, and require manual updates as they don't 'learn' from new information. Difficulty identifying inconsistencies within the model, or between the model and related knowledge autonomously.

  • Statistical nature with uncertainty — Problems characterised by significant uncertainty, yet involving discoverable rules and causal chains that can be modeled

Use Case Requirements:

  • Validated pain points — Pain points are serious enough that practitioners are willing to collaborate and ultimately engage in commercial pilot contracts

  • Strategic fit with our system’s capabilities and long term product vision

  • Identified pilot users — You have established contacts with industry practitioners actively using the relevant workflows, who are interested in validating solutions and quality checking the model

Engagement Process

Our collaboration follows a structured 4-stage development cycle:

  • Stage 1: Opportunity identification - We establish together whether this is a relevant use case for us, and sketch the initial solution architecture.

  • Stage 2: Validation - The goal of this stage is to establish the problem solution fit, commercial viability, and the ICP (ideal customer profile): with your help we will identify and jointly interview numerous practitioners, and ideally secure pilot user engagements.

  • Stage 3: Specification & Implementation - You collaborate with our engineers to translate the validated solution architecture into a working model within our system, and participate actively in user testing with our pilot users.

  • Stage 4: Production - Transitioning from pilot to sustained, production-grade usage. You support the integration into users' existing tools and help identify opportunities for expansion.

Collaboration & Compensation

Our compensation model is designed to support you through the early exploration phases while offering significant upside for successful outcomes. Our compensation has two components:

  • Competitive per-diem rates and engagement via self-employment/contractor, billed via time tracking to PlantingSpace AG (a Swiss company).

  • Participation in Commercial Success: Opportunity to participate in gross profit sharing from jointly established user engagements.

Next Steps

If you have expertise in a relevant domain and connections to potential pilot users, we would love to hear from you. To discuss a potential collaboration, please complete the application form, including:

  • A brief description of the specific domain challenge and concrete model you're considering

  • A summary of your level of expertise and relevant experience within the concrete project scope

  • High-level outline of your industry connections and potential access to relevant pilot users

We review all proposals, and will reach out to schedule an initial conversation if there is a strategic fit.

jobs.title: Analytic Learning Algorithm Research
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We're building a system that represents domain knowledge as modular probabilistic models — making analysis rigorous and transparent. Users can connect these models flexibly into larger structures. The system enforces consistency across them, and propagates uncertainty through each step. Our first applications are in finance and scientific research, with use cases ranging from equity valuation and distress monitoring, to particle physics.

We are looking for full-time researchers to contribute to the development and analysis of our learning algorithms. You will work on interesting theoretical problems with immediate applicability to implementation of our system.

Our team works fully remotely, and mostly within the CET timezone.

Useful experience

  • Development of mathematical analysis methods, for example: optimal transport, information geometry, continuous optimization methods

  • Analysis of probabilistic graphical models, including factor graphs

  • Implementation of tractable density estimators (normalising flows, autoregressive density models, probabilistic circuits)

  • Translation between equational reasoning and code implementation

  • Mathematics, Computer Science, or Statistics advanced degree (with PhD or equivalent research experience)

Responsibilities

  • Develop numerical-analytical models of learning in our system

  • Connect our research to existing literature

  • Prove properties of algorithms and design experiments to validate results empirically

  • Leverage the expertise of other team members effectively

  • Write clean and well documented code

  • Help other team members to deliver on their goals

How we work

  • Hierarchical goals, not personal hierarchies: We organise around a transparent tree of goals and tasks. Every quarter we plan milestone goals, which branch down into smaller and smaller tasks. This tree is the foundation of how we organise, not a side tool.

jobs.title: Backend Software Engineering
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We're building a system that represents domain knowledge as modular probabilistic models — making analysis rigorous and transparent. Users can connect these models flexibly into larger structures. The system enforces consistency across them, and propagates uncertainty through each step. Our first applications are in finance and scientific research, with use cases ranging from equity valuation and distress monitoring, to particle physics.

We are looking for strong software engineers to build our production system. This opening is focused on building a robust and scalable backend hosting our reasoning engine. It is ideal for an engineer with a deep interest in systems architecture, reliability and scalability. You will be able to choose how close to the reasoning engine or the infrastructure you want to work, and be exposed to a novel class of reasoning models.

Essential experience

  • Software engineering in a collaborative, commercial environment, working on large codebases and using practices like CI/CD, testing, and code reviews.

  • Functional/typed languages, e.g. Rust, OCaml, Clojure, C++, or Haskell, and a willingness to learn and work with Julia, TypeScript and Rust.

  • Scalable services development including databases, networking and computing across architectures.

  • Implementation of observability across the stack.

  • CI/CD pipelines with complex trade-offs between correctness and development experience.

Useful experience

  • Hosting of machine learning models, or other computationally heavy services.

  • Development of infrastructure with Terraform and Kubernetes.
